deviations.behavior_difference: Zapbrew exposes an explicit per-formula step-journal terminal: success transfers and removes its backup root before reporting completion; Homebrew does not expose this journal ownership contract.
deviations.safety_risk: A stale root can retain overwritten bytes; clearing state before ownership transfer can lose the cleanup target.
deviations.threat_model: An interrupted or failed cleanup after structured file mutation, including hostile or inconsistent prefix entries.
deviations.invariant: A successful install keeps the committed keg and links active, removes the step-journal root, and leaves the journal empty.
deviations.reproduction: Run the W4 success workload and inspect replacement bytes, keg and link state, and absence of `.zapbrew-step-journal-*`.
deviations.alternatives_rejected: A borrowed cleanup path plus a later clear was rejected because it split one terminal transition; no journal was rejected because overwrite rollback would lose prior bytes.

deviations.behavior_difference: Zapbrew isolates structured-step compensation per formula while leaving external Run and maintenance effects outside compensation; Homebrew does not expose an equivalent journal boundary.
deviations.safety_risk: Cross-formula inverse replay can undo a formula that already completed successfully or report the wrong residue owner.
deviations.threat_model: A later selected formula fails after an earlier selected formula completed; external commands can have effects that are not reversible file mutations.
deviations.invariant: No journal records or replays another formula’s file-system effects; the first formula remains committed when the second rolls back.
deviations.reproduction: Run `postinstall_failure_does_not_roll_back_prior_formula` and `run_and_maintenance_effects_survive_rollback`; the first formula stays committed when the second rolls back, and generic Run plus deferred maintenance markers survive structured compensation.
deviations.alternatives_rejected: A shared journal was rejected because it couples independent formula terminals; pretending external commands are reversible was rejected because their effects have no reliable inverse.

deviations.behavior_difference: Zapbrew treats step-journal-root removal after commit as typed cleanup and preserves the committed installation; Homebrew does not expose this post-commit journal cleanup contract.
deviations.safety_risk: Rolling back after commit can replace the working keg with stale state; ignoring residue can leak backup data.
deviations.threat_model: Journal-root removal fails after the keg and links have crossed the commit boundary.
deviations.invariant: CleanupIncomplete names the committed keg and surviving root; the new keg and links remain active and no pre-commit rollback runs.
deviations.reproduction: Arm the one-shot cleanup failure and run `step_root_cleanup_failure_keeps_new_keg_active`; inspect the typed error, active links, new bytes, and one surviving root.
deviations.alternatives_rejected: Rollback-on-cleanup-error was rejected because commit is irreversible at this boundary; silent cleanup failure was rejected because it hides retained backup data.

deviations.behavior_difference: Zapbrew gives each selected postinstall formula an explicit journal and typed rollback or cleanup residue attribution; Homebrew does not expose this lifecycle as a public error contract.
deviations.safety_risk: A shared or uncleared journal can attribute residue to the wrong keg or undo a prior formula.
deviations.threat_model: Multiple selected formulae execute structured postinstall steps, with success, execution failure, or cleanup failure on any selected keg.
deviations.invariant: Each selected formula owns one terminal journal; success removes its root, failure restores only that keg, and residue names that keg.
deviations.reproduction: Run the postinstall integration suite; observe successful cleanup, selected-keg rollback, and `CleanupIncomplete` naming the selected keg and surviving journal-root symlink.
deviations.alternatives_rejected: One shared journal was rejected because formula effects can cross-contaminate; untyped cleanup was rejected because it loses keg attribution.

deviations.behavior_difference: Zapbrew replays explicit structured-step inverses before the outer transaction rollback and reports surviving paths; Homebrew does not expose this typed inverse-replay contract.
deviations.safety_risk: Wrong replay order can restore stale bytes over newer state or leave a failed keg and links active.
deviations.threat_model: A structured step fails after one or more confined file-system mutations; rollback operations can also fail.
deviations.invariant: Every inverse is attempted in reverse order before outer rollback; clean rollback returns the original error, and residue becomes one RollbackIncomplete.
deviations.reproduction: Run the W4 rollback workload, `rollback_replays_multiple_inverses_in_reverse_order`, and `inverse_failure_merges_into_outer_rollback_incomplete`; inspect restored original bytes after reverse replay and the merged original command error plus surviving path after inverse failure.
deviations.alternatives_rejected: Best-effort deletion without inverses was rejected because it cannot restore overwritten bytes; independent error returns were rejected because they can hide rollback residue.
